In control mice, the odor-related response did not produce the same combination of extreme population activation and subsequent loss of muscle tone.

sources.teaching_note: The recorded neurons also became more synchronized during odor-associated cataplexy. A downstream target could receive a more concentrated inhibitory input when many connected neurons become active together.

sources.source_legend: Video 1.Male-female pairs at ZT 20 under infrared light.Normally fed or yeast-deprived iso31 males were paired with normally fed female partners. While most normally fed males were courting, the majority of yeast-deprived males were inactive.
sources.teaching_note: The source recording compares these social conditions during the night under infrared illumination. The researchers separately scored sleeping and courting, rather than treating every movement as the same behavior. Yeast-deprived males still showed daytime courtship, indicating that the nighttime difference involved behavioral allocation rather than complete loss of the courtship repertoire.

sources.teaching_note: The source recording shows a sleep-deprived pair in the behavioral assay. sources.source_legend: Figure 2—video 1.Time-lapse bioluminescence imaging of a coronal SCN slice of a Sik3+/+; Per2 Luc/Luc mouse.Exposure time for a single image was 20 min, and time-lapse images were captured for 4 consecutive days. sources.teaching_note: The source recording shows a normal mouse SCN slice across successive cycles. Individual cells change their light output, and their timing is coordinated enough to produce an organized population rhythm. The changing brightness reports the molecular reporter rather than ordinary neural electrical spikes or a flash of calcium associated with a single action potential.

sources.source_legend: Figure 2—video 2.Time-lapse bioluminescence imaging of a SCN slice of a Sik3-/-; Per2 Luc/Luc mouse.Exposure time for a single image was 55 min, and time-lapse images were captured for 3 consecutive days. Note that Per2 Luc rhythms were desynchronized among individual cells in the SCN.
sources.teaching_note: The source movie follows the SIK3-deficient preparation using the same PER2-linked light reporter as the normal slice. A population image can lose a coherent rhythm when individual cells peak at different times. Single-cell tracking showed that the altered signal involved instability and desynchronization rather than simply disappearance of all cellular clock activity.

sources.source_legend: Video 1.Principal Component Analysis of CK1δ normal modes.The 1st principal mode of motion corresponds to an ‘open-and-close’ movement of the kinase, achieved mainly by dislocation of the N-terminal lobe (N-lobe) with respect to the top of the helix F. sources.source_legend: Video 1.Flies exhibit sleep following 2.5 hr SD terminating at ZT1.5 Sped up video recording of 4.5 hr of rebound of 36 WT flies following SD from ZT23-ZT1.5.Hours post SD are indicated in red in the bottom right corner. Flies exhibit little movement throughout the 4.5 hr following SD indicating sleep.
sources.teaching_note: The researchers measured rebound relative to baseline sleep at the same time of day. This comparison matters because an animal may normally sleep more in the morning than in the evening. Additional sleep after deprivation must be separated from the daily sleep pattern that would have occurred even without the experimental interruption.

sources.source_legend: Video 2.Flies are active following 2.5 hr SD terminating at ZT9.5 Sped up video recording of 4.5 hr of rebound of 36 WT flies following SD from ZT7-ZT9.5.Hours post SD are indicated in red in the bottom right corner. After a brief period of immobility flies exhibit high activity (low sleep) preceding lights on.
sources.teaching_note: The ellipsoid-body neurons also responded differently: the calcium increase observed after morning sleep loss was not present in the same way after evening loss. Clock-neuron manipulations changed this time-dependent regulation. The homeostatic circuit's cellular response was therefore being programmed by circadian input, rather than responding only to the number of minutes awake.
